# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask config-docs` from the config file's JSON Schema; do not edit. -->

The configuration file, version 1. Only secrets (`token`, `secret_token`, `auth_token`, `admin.token`) and fields holding URLs or file paths expand `${env:NAME}` and `${file:PATH}` references; every other value is literal.

Each table lists a section's keys with their type and default. A key without a default is optional unless marked **required**. The JSON Schema itself is [`schema/tgin.v1.schema.json`](../schema/tgin.v1.schema.json); `tgin config schema` prints it.

## Top level

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `admin` | [Admin](#admin) | `{"listen":["127.0.0.1:9090"],"public_metrics":false}` | The admin HTTP server: health, metrics and the management API. |
| `bots` | list of [Bot](#bot) | `[]` | The Telegram bots updates come from. |
| `consumers` | map of names matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` to [Consumer](#consumer) | `{}` | Where updates go, by name. |
| `log` | [Log](#log) | `{"format":"text","level":"info"}` | Logging, to stdout. |
| `reload` | [Reload](#reload) | `{"debounce":"500ms","drain_timeout":"30s","watch":true}` | Hot reload of the config file. |
| `runtime` | [Runtime](#runtime) | `{"lame_duck":"5s","shutdown_grace":"15s","worker_threads":"auto"}` | Process settings. `worker_threads` takes effect after a restart; a shutdown uses the `lame_duck` and `shutdown_grace` of the config in effect when it begins. |
| `server` | [Server](#server) |  | The data plane: webhook ingress and pull consumers. Omitted, tgin serves neither. |
| `version` | `1` | **required** | The config format version; must be 1. |

## `Admin`

The admin HTTP server: health, metrics and the management API.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `listen` | list of string | `["127.0.0.1:9090"]` | Addresses to listen on, as `ip:port`. A non-loopback address needs `token`. |
| `public_metrics` | boolean | `false` | Serve `/metrics` without the token. |
| `token` | [Secret](#secret) |  | Bearer token for the admin API. |

## `Secret`

A secret. Supports `${env:NAME}` and `${file:PATH}` (relative to the config file); `$${` is a literal `${`.

Type: string (not empty).

## `Bot`

One Telegram bot.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api_url` | string (not empty) | `https://api.telegram.org` | Bot API base URL. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`. |
| `ingress` | [Ingress](#ingress) |  | How updates arrive; at most one. Omitted, the bot receives none. |
| `name` | string (matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`) | **required** | Unique bot name, used in metrics and logs. |
| `routes` | list of [Route](#route) | `[]` | Rules in order; the first match wins. |
| `token` | [Secret](#secret) | **required** | The bot token. |

## `Ingress`

One of:

- `long_poll`: [LongPoll](#longpoll) — Poll Telegram with `getUpdates`.
- `webhook`: [Webhook](#webhook) — Receive updates on the data-plane server.

## `LongPoll`

Long polling: tgin calls `getUpdates` on the Bot API.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowed_updates` | list of string |  | Update types to receive. Omitted, Telegram's default applies. |
| `delete_webhook_on_start` | boolean | `true` | Call `deleteWebhook` (keeping pending updates) before polling, and again when a poll finds a webhook set. Off, an active webhook stops the polling until something else deletes it. |
| `limit` | integer (at least 1, at most 100) | `100` | Updates per `getUpdates` call, 1 to 100. |
| `timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | `30s` | `getUpdates` long-poll timeout; at least 1 s. |

## `Duration`

A duration such as `500ms`, `1.5s`, `5m` or `1h 30m`, or `0`. Month (`M`) and year (`y`) units are rejected.

One of:

- string
- `0`

Examples: `30s`, `1.5s`, `5m`.

## `Webhook`

Telegram posts updates to the data plane.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowed_updates` | list of string |  | Update types to receive. Omitted, Telegram's default applies. |
| `certificate_file` | string (not empty) |  | Self-signed certificate to upload with `setWebhook`; needs `register: true`. A relative path is relative to the config file's directory. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`. |
| `drop_pending_updates` | boolean | `false` | Telegram's `drop_pending_updates` for `setWebhook`. |
| `ip_address` | IP address |  | Telegram's `ip_address` for `setWebhook`. |
| `ip_allowlist` | [IpAllowlist](#ipallowlist) | `none` | Who may post updates: `none` (anyone), `telegram` (Telegram's published networks) or a list of networks. |
| `max_connections` | integer (at least 1, at most 100) |  | Telegram's `max_connections`, 1 to 100. |
| `path` | string (not empty) |  | HTTP path updates are posted to. Omitted, `/webhook/<bot name>`. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`. |
| `public_url` | string (not empty) |  | The public HTTPS base URL Telegram reaches tgin at; `setWebhook` registers it followed by `path`. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`. |
| `register` | boolean | `false` | Call `setWebhook` at start; needs `public_url`. |
| `secret_token` | [WebhookSecret](#webhooksecret) | `auto` | `auto` (derived from the bot token), `none`, or the secret Telegram must send. |

## `IpAllowlist`

One of:

- `none` — Any client may post.
- `telegram` — Telegram's published webhook networks.
- list of [Cidr](#cidr)

## `Cidr`

An IP network such as `10.0.0.0/8`, or a single address.

Type: string.

Examples: `10.0.0.0/8`, `2001:db8::/32`.

## `WebhookSecret`

One of:

- `auto` — Derived from the bot token (HMAC-SHA256); the same on every restart and replica.
- `none` — Send and check no secret.
- [Secret](#secret)

## `Route`

One routing rule.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `match` | [Match](#match) |  | When the rule applies. Omitted, it matches every update. |
| `to` | list of [Target](#target) | **required** | Where matching updates go; every entry receives the update. |

## `Match`

Rule predicates: values within a list are alternatives, fields must all hold, and an empty list matches anything.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `callback_data` | [TextMatch](#textmatch) |  | Callback query data. |
| `chat_ids` | list of integer | `[]` | Chat ids. |
| `chat_types` | list of [ChatType](#chattype) | `[]` | Chat types. |
| `commands` | list of string (matching `^/?[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,32}$`) | `[]` | Commands, with or without the leading `/`: 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits or `_`, with no `@bot` suffix. |
| `text` | [TextMatch](#textmatch) |  | Message text or caption. |
| `update_types` | list of string | `[]` | Update types such as `message` or `callback_query`. |
| `user_ids` | list of integer | `[]` | Sender user ids. |

## `TextMatch`

A text match; each list is non-empty.

One of:

- `prefix`: list of string — Starts with any of these (case-sensitive).
- `regex`: list of string — Any of these regexes matches somewhere in the text.
- `equals`: list of string — Equals any of these exactly.

## `ChatType`

One of:

- `private`
- `group`
- `supergroup`
- `channel`

## `Target`

A consumer name, `{split: …}` (one child receives the update) or `{all: […]}` (every child does).

One of:

- string — A consumer name.
- `split`: [Split](#split)
- `all`: list of [Target](#target)

## `Split`

Exactly one child of `among` receives each update.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `among` | list of [Target](#target) | **required** | The children: consumer names or nested targets. |
| `strategy` | [SplitStrategy](#splitstrategy) | **required** | How a split picks its child. |
| `weights` | list of integer (at least 1) |  | One weight per `among` entry, each above 0; only with `weighted`. |

## `SplitStrategy`

How a split picks its child.

One of:

- `round_robin` — Each child in turn.
- `hash_chat` — Sticky by chat (or user); round robin without either.
- `weighted` — Smooth weighted round robin over `weights`.

## `Consumer`

One of:

- `pull`: [Pull](#pull) — Bots fetch updates from tgin with `getUpdates`.
- `push`: [Push](#push) — tgin posts updates to HTTP endpoints.

## `Pull`

Bots fetch updates from tgin with `getUpdates` on `/c/<consumer>/getUpdates` and on each alias.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aliases` | list of string (not empty) | `[]` | Extra HTTP paths serving this consumer. Each supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`. |
| `auth_token` | [Secret](#secret) |  | Bearer token pollers must send. |
| `capacity` | integer (at least 1) | `10000` | Most queued updates. |
| `capacity_bytes` | [ByteSize](#bytesize) | `64MiB` | Most queued bytes. |
| `lease_timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | `2m` | How long a fetched update waits for its acknowledgement before another poll may receive it. |
| `on_full` | [OnFull](#onfull) | `backpressure` | What a full queue does with a new update. |
| `ordering` | [Ordering](#ordering) | `none` | The order a consumer hands out updates in. |

## `ByteSize`

A size of at least 1 MiB: bytes, or a number with `B`, `KiB`, `MiB` or `GiB`.

One of:

- integer (at least 1048576)
- string

Examples: `64MiB`, `1024KiB`, `1048576`.

## `OnFull`

What a full queue does with a new update.

One of:

- `backpressure` — Refuse it; the source retries later.
- `drop_oldest` — Evict the oldest queued updates.

## `Ordering`

The order a consumer hands out updates in.

One of:

- `none` — Queue order, any number per chat at once.
- `per_chat` — One update per chat (or user) in flight at a time; updates with neither are never held back.

## `Push`

tgin posts each update to HTTP endpoints, with retries and a circuit breaker per endpoint.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `balance` | [Balance](#balance) | `round_robin` | How a push consumer picks the endpoint for each attempt, among those whose circuit breaker admits a request. |
| `breaker` | [Breaker](#breaker) | `{"failure_threshold":5,"open_for":"30s"}` | Per-endpoint circuit breaker. |
| `capacity` | integer (at least 1) | `10000` | Most queued updates. |
| `capacity_bytes` | [ByteSize](#bytesize) | `64MiB` | Most queued bytes. |
| `endpoints` | list of [Endpoint](#endpoint) | **required** | Where updates are posted; at least one. |
| `max_in_flight` | integer (at least 1) | `32` | Most deliveries at once over all endpoints, counting those waiting to retry. |
| `on_full` | [OnFull](#onfull) | `backpressure` | What a full queue does with a new update. |
| `ordering` | [Ordering](#ordering) | `none` | The order a consumer hands out updates in. |
| `retry` | [Retry](#retry) | `{"initial":"1s","max":"1m","max_age":"1h","max_attempts":10}` | Retries of failed deliveries. |

## `Balance`

How a push consumer picks the endpoint for each attempt, among those whose circuit breaker admits a request.

One of:

- `round_robin` — Each endpoint in turn.
- `hash_chat` — Sticky by chat (or user); round robin without either.
- `least_in_flight` — The endpoint with the fewest requests in flight.

## `Breaker`

Per-endpoint circuit breaker.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `failure_threshold` | integer (at least 1) | `5` | Consecutive transient failures (408, 429, 5xx, timeouts, network errors) that open the breaker; at least 1. |
| `open_for` | [Duration](#duration) | `30s` | How long the breaker stays open. |

## `Endpoint`

One downstream URL.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `secret_token` | [Secret](#secret) |  | Sent as `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`. |
| `timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | `10s` | Per-request timeout. |
| `url` | string (not empty) | **required** | `http` or `https` URL. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`. |

## `Retry`

Retries of failed deliveries.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `initial` | [Duration](#duration) | `1s` | First backoff. |
| `max` | [Duration](#duration) | `1m` | Longest backoff. |
| `max_age` | [Duration](#duration) | `1h` | Age after which the update is dead-lettered. |
| `max_attempts` | integer (at least 1) | `10` | Attempts before the update is dead-lettered; at least 1. |

## `Log`

Logging, to stdout.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `format` | [LogFormat](#logformat) | `text` | Log line format; a change takes effect after a restart. |
| `level` | [LogLevel](#loglevel) | `info` | The most verbose level logged; a reload applies it. A non-empty `RUST_LOG` overrides it. |

## `LogFormat`

One of:

- `text`
- `json`

## `LogLevel`

One of:

- `trace`
- `debug`
- `info`
- `warn`
- `error`

## `Reload`

Hot reload of the config file.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `debounce` | [Duration](#duration) | `500ms` | Quiet time after a change before reloading; at least 10ms. |
| `drain_timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | `30s` | How long a removed consumer drains before it is dropped. |
| `watch` | boolean | `true` | Reload when the config file changes. |

## `Runtime`

Process settings. `worker_threads` takes effect after a restart; a shutdown uses the `lame_duck` and `shutdown_grace` of the config in effect when it begins.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lame_duck` | [Duration](#duration) | `5s` | How long, once shutdown begins, tgin keeps serving while readiness reports "not ready", before it stops ingesting; skipped without a `server` block. |
| `shutdown_grace` | [Duration](#duration) | `15s` | How long shutdown waits for queues to drain. |
| `worker_threads` | [WorkerThreads](#workerthreads) | `auto` | Tokio worker threads: `auto` (one per CPU) or a count. |

## `WorkerThreads`

One of:

- `auto` — One per CPU.
- integer (at least 1)

## `Server`

The data-plane HTTP server.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `header_read_timeout` | [Duration](#duration) | `10s` | How long a client may take to send the request headers. |
| `listen` | list of string | `["0.0.0.0:8080"]` | Addresses to listen on, as `ip:port`. |
| `max_connections` | integer (at least 1) | `10000` | Most open connections. |
| `tls` | [Tls](#tls) |  | Serve HTTPS with these files. Turning TLS on or off takes effect after a restart. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of [Cidr](#cidr) | `[]` | Proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted, as networks. |

## `Tls`

The data plane's certificate. Every config reload reads both files again and swaps the certificate in if they changed.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cert_file` | string (not empty) | **required** | PEM certificate chain file; a relative path is relative to the config file's directory. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`. |
| `key_file` | string (not empty) | **required** | PEM private key file; a relative path is relative to the config file's directory. Supports `${env:…}` and `${file:…}`. |
